# rustinion_audit_stream_destination (Resource)

Manages a Rustinion audit-log streaming export destination: continuous delivery of this tenant's own admin_audit_log events to an external SIEM — a generic HMAC-signed webhook, a native Splunk HTTP Event Collector endpoint, or a native RFC 5424 syslog forwarder. One destination per tenant.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)

### Optional

- `destination_type` (String) "webhook" (default, a generic HMAC-signed delivery), "splunk_hec" (a native Splunk HTTP Event Collector client), or "syslog" (a native RFC 5424 syslog forwarder over TCP, RFC 6587 framed, optionally TLS). Fixed at creation — switching types means destroying and recreating this resource.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Defaults to true on create.
- `hec_endpoint` (String) Required for destination_type = "splunk_hec": the customer's own full HEC URL, e.g. "https://splunk.example.com:8088/services/collector/event". Not used for "webhook".
- `hec_index` (String) splunk_hec only, optional: Splunk applies its own default index when this is unset.
- `hec_sourcetype` (String) splunk_hec only, optional: Splunk applies its own default sourcetype when this is unset.
- `hec_token` (String, Sensitive) Required for destination_type = "splunk_hec": the customer's own HEC token, sent as the "Authorization: Splunk <token>" header. Unlike signing_secret, this is a customer-supplied secret the API freely returns on every read, so it round-trips normally through this attribute (no state-preservation workaround needed) — but it is not updatable via Update (no rotation without recreate, matching signing_secret's own stated v1 scope cut).
- `syslog_host` (String) Required for destination_type = "syslog": the receiver's hostname or IP. Not used for the other two types.
- `syslog_port` (Number) Required for destination_type = "syslog", 1-65535.
- `syslog_use_tls` (Boolean) syslog only. true wraps the TCP connection in TLS (server-certificate validation only, no client-certificate/mutual-TLS support in v1) before sending; false (the default when set for a syslog destination) sends over plain TCP. syslog has no secret/token concept at all — this flag, or bare network trust when it's false, is the entire real "authentication" story for this delivery type.
- `webhook_url` (String) Required for destination_type = "webhook"; not used for "splunk_hec".

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_delivered_at` (String) RFC3339 timestamp of the last successfully delivered event, or this destination's own creation time if nothing has been delivered yet.
- `last_delivery_error` (String) The most recent delivery failure's own detail, empty if the destination is currently healthy.
- `last_delivery_failed_at` (String) RFC3339 timestamp of the most recent delivery failure, empty if the destination is currently healthy.
- `signing_secret` (String, Sensitive) webhook only. Server-generated HMAC-SHA256 secret for verifying the X-Rustinion-Signature header on every delivery. Only ever known at creation time — the API never returns it again, so this value is preserved from state on every later refresh rather than re-read (there is nothing to re-read). Rotation is not supported in v1: change this by tainting and recreating the resource. Always empty for a splunk_hec destination.
